The State of AI Voices in Games
Skip to content
AI x Gaming
The State of AI Voices in Games
By Mike Markin •   November 10, 2026
Source:
Keywords Studios
AI voice for games has grown well past basic speech synthesis and is already live in several AAA games. For NHL 27,
EA confirmed it used AI
to expand on more than 50 recording sessions, with the consent and continued involvement of commentators John Buccigross and Darren Pang. In Fortnite, AI-generated Darth Vader dialogue prompted
SAG-AFTRA’s unfair labor practice charge
against Epic Games subsidiary Llama Productions, alleging replacement of performers’ work without notice or bargaining.
Choosing a provider now means deciding where the models run, how generated lines fit into production, what consent and union agreements require, and whether new capabilities justify the risks to player trust and performer relationships. So where is AI voice gaining ground? How mature are its different applications? And which companies are positioned to benefit?
The Case for AI Voice
AI voice gives studios a powerful economic incentive to replace paid recording work.
SAG-AFTRA’s standard session minimum
is $1,169 for up to four hours, while
ElevenLabs’ published v4 API rate
works out to about $4.80 per hour of generated speech, based on ElevenLabs’ estimated audio duration. The session fee pays an actor to perform under direction, while the API rate covers raw generated audio, which still needs direction, editing, review and voice licensing at extra cost.
Lower-cost speech generation gives studios more flexibility in allocating voice budgets. They can reduce repetitive recording, extend spoken dialogue to more languages, or test lines before paying for final performances.
However, when generated speech meets a game’s requirements, studios can substitute synthesis for recording sessions they would otherwise commission, putting performers’ current and future work at risk. Across the wider voiceover industry, 21% of respondents said they had
knowingly lost a job to a synthetic voice
. Respondents described clients explicitly telling them they were being replaced because synthetic voices were “faster and cheaper.” Hollywood voice actors
are split over AI voice cloning
: many report declining opportunities and worry about training their own replacements.
Source:
NAVA
Practical Application
Extending Recorded Performances
AI can supplement a performer’s recordings when a game needs large volumes of predictable variations. In sports commentary, for example, player names must be delivered with different levels of excitement and woven into commentary recorded across multiple sessions.
For
EA Sports FC
, commentator Guy Mowbray
authorized an AI recreation of his voice
to replace months of tedious recording work generating names from the game’s roster of more than 20,000 players. The AI extends an agreed performance across repetitive material, while the rest still comes from Mowbray’s own recordings.
This flexibility becomes more valuable as games evolve into live services. New content and seasonal updates create an ongoing need for dialogue, while last-minute script changes can force teams to rebook actors. With the performer’s permission, studios can generate additions and revisions from existing recordings and keep voice production in step with updates.
Localization
AI voice localization spans text-to-speech, speech-to-speech conversion, and AI dubbing that uses voice cloning to keep an actor’s voice across languages. Companies such as ElevenLabs develop the underlying models,
offering dubbing tools
that combine translation, voice cloning and synchronization across more than 90 languages. Localization providers increasingly license that technology or partner with its developers to build it into their workflows and connect it to the engines studios use.
Gridly
, whose plugins sync translated text into
Unity
and
Unreal Engine
, uses Amazon’s text-to-speech voices to generate voice-over for each character next to every translated line so teams can check timing in each language before recording.
Source:
Gridly
Altagram’s
Alocai
takes localization requests from Unity through the
Dialogue System for Unity
add-on and checks the recordings that come back, transcribing each take and flagging mismatches against the script.
Other providers include
Side
, which combines its casting and recording studios with a Synthetic Voice Design service, while
BLEND
offers 1,300 contracted voice actors in 120 languages alongside AI voice production.
Prototyping
Studios have long relied on “scratch tracks,” often recorded by developers themselves, so writers, animators, and level and cinematic designers can test pacing, timing, and triggers before booking actors. With AI, a rewritten line can be regenerated in seconds, in a consistent character voice, while scenes are still changing. Among game audio professionals who have adopted generative AI,
43% use it for placeholder dialogue
. Players are comparatively accepting as well. In GameDiscoverCo’s July 2026 survey of Steam players, prototyping and placeholder assets drew mentions as an
acceptable use of AI
, behind only coding tools.
For
The Blood of Dawnwalker
, CEO and game director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz said “the recordings are one of the biggest costs when you’re doing a story-driven RPG.” The studio used
AI-generated voices
to iterate on the story, then replaced them with actors once the scenes were locked.
The risk is that generated voice lines reach players. Embark shipped licensed text-to-speech voices for less essential lines in Arc Raiders, then
re-recorded some of them with professional actors
after player criticism. CEO Patrick Söderlund conceded that
“there is a quality difference.”
In Tomb Raider IV–VI Remastered,
Aspyr removed all AI voiceover
content in a hotfix after Françoise Cadol, the French voice of Lara Croft, accused the studio of replicating her voice without consent and took legal action.
